headline: Every major back above its 200-day line while ETF desks and exchange flows point the other way
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it's unusually clean today: BTC, ETH, SOL, BNB, and XRP all sit above their 200-day moving averages with golden crosses confirmed. DOGE and ADA are the two holdouts, both still below trend and both showing the largest drawdowns from their 12-month highs (-70.0% and -77.1% respectively). That's seven assets, five above the line, two below, and it's the below-trend pair that's also furthest from their highs. Read that as a market where the majors have repaired their long-term structure while the next tier down hasn't caught up.

Momentum is where it gets more interesting. Every asset in the board is showing MACD below its signal line even as RSI readings sit in the high 50s to low 60s (BTC 60.0, ETH 63.9, SOL 59.0, XRP 61.0). That's a textbook divergence: price and RSI say the move is still constructive, MACD says the short-term thrust has cooled. Worth naming plainly since it's uniform across the board, not a one-off. BTC itself is the clearest illustration of window disagreement: up 2.7% on the day, up 24.3% on the month, but down 0.9% on the week. Three different stories depending on which clock you check, and none of them wrong.

Positioning tells you who's paying for this. BTC funding on OKX sits at 0.0047% per 8 hours (5.2% annualized), modest by crypto standards, with open interest at $2.09B and a long/short ratio of 1.23, tilted long but not extreme. SOL and XRP funding runs hotter (11.0% annualized each) with long/short ratios of 1.87 and 1.96, more crowded on the long side. The liquidation tape backs this up: BTC saw $1.6M in short liquidations against $242K in longs over the past hour, meaning the squeeze that drove today's 2.7% pop wiped out shorts, not longs. SOL's hourly liquidations show the same lopsided pattern ($1.07M shorts vs $39K longs). Crowded-and-paying-up is a fragile setup by definition; it doesn't say which way it breaks, only that there's more to unwind on one side.

Flows are where the tension sharpens. BTC ETFs printed a $13.2M outflow on 11 Sep 2026, and the five-session net is a outflow of $288.1M with four straight days in the same direction, a real institutional bid stepping back. ETH ETFs did the opposite: $216.4M in on 11 Sep 2026, $222.8M over five sessions, though same_direction_days of 1 means that's mostly one big day, not a building trend. Meanwhile whale wallets moved $5.03M net onto exchanges over the last 72 hours, with the week ending Sep 14 showing $725M onto exchanges, reversing the prior week's $347M move off exchanges. Stablecoin float is up 1.25% over 30 days to $310.1B, so there's dry powder sitting on the sidelines, but the near-term whale trend and the BTC ETF trend are both pointing the same direction: away from the asset, at least for now.

Sentiment sits at 57, labeled Greed, near the middle of its 30-day range of 31 to 74. That's the crowd feeling reasonably good, which lines up with the price action (every major asset green on the day) but sits awkwardly next to a BTC ETF desk that's pulled money for four straight sessions and whale wallets nudging coin onto exchanges into that same stretch. The tape and the mood aren't shouting at each other, but they're not singing the same tune either.

What's worth watching from here: whether BTC funding stays contained near its current 5.2% annualized or starts climbing toward the 11% levels seen in SOL and XRP, whether the ETH ETF inflow on 11 Sep turns into a second or third same-direction day rather than staying a one-day event, and whether the weekly whale flow for the week ending Sep 14 (net onto exchanges) gets echoed or reversed in the next weekly print. Any of those flipping would say more about where this stands than today's single green candle does.
